User: I have a legal situation I need help thinking through. It's related to contract dispute with a former employer. I'm working with Sarah Chen from Hart & Associates; our next step is housing court. Timeline: The judge set a status conference in two months.. The other party is my former business partner. We're in Maricopa County, Arizona. I have documentation but I'm not sure what else the court will want. I'd like to know what I should ask my lawyer regarding my rights and what the next steps typically

look like. This is private legal business.
Assistant: Thanks — I won’t share this. I’m not your lawyer, but I can help you prepare so your meeting with Sarah Chen is efficient and thorough. Below is a practical checklist of questions to ask her, documents and tasks to prepare before the status conference, what the court typically wants at a status conference, and common next steps and options so you can have a focused conversation.

If anything below looks off (for example, if this isn’t actually a landlord

/tenant “housing” matter) tell me and I’ll tailor it.

What to ask your lawyer (direct, high‑priority questions)
- Case basics and theory
  - What claims should we be asserting (contract breach, accountings, conversion, other)? What defenses should we expect from the other side?
  - What specific rights and remedies am I likely entitled to under Arizona law (damages, specific performance, injunctive relief, costs/attorney’s fees)?
- Status conference & procedure
  - What will happen at the status conference

? Will we need a joint status report or prescribed disclosures beforehand?
  - What schedule should we propose for discovery, motions, and trial? What deadlines will the court likely set?
- Evidence and proof
  - What documents and evidence will be most important and how should they be authenticated (business records affidavits, witness testimony, admission documents)?
  - Do we need expert witnesses (accountant, valuation expert)? If so, when should we retain them?
- Filing strategy & motions
  - Should we

file any motions before or at the status conference (motion to dismiss, motion for partial summary judgment, temporary relief)?
  - Should we consider a counterclaim or setoff?
- Discovery and preservation
  - What should we do immediately to preserve evidence (emails, bank records, devices, communications)? Are there steps to prevent spoliation?
  - What discovery tools are likely (written discovery, document requests, subpoenas, depositions) and any limits in Arizona or the local court?
- Settlement & al

ternatives
  - What are realistic settlement options and when should we push for mediation? Would the court likely order or encourage mediation?
  - What is our bottom line and how should settlement offers be handled?
- Costs and timeline
  - What is the likely timeline (discovery period length, motion windows, trial scheduling) and estimated costs to trial?
  - How do your billing practices and retainer work? What additional fees (experts, filing, subpoenas) should I expect?
- Risks and outcomes
  - What a

re the best-case, worst-case, and most likely outcomes?
  - If we win, how is judgment enforced in Arizona (collection, liens, garnishment)? If we lose, what are appeal options/timelines?
- Communication & logistics
  - How will you keep me informed (email, phone)? What do you need from me now and before the status conference?
  - Who else from the firm will handle the case and will you be at the status conference/trial?

Documents and materials to bring/send to your lawyer now
- The written contract(s) at

issue, all amendments and exhibits
- All communications with the former partner (emails, texts, messaging, letters) in chronological order
- Financial records: invoices, receipts, bank statements, payment records, accounting ledgers
- Any lease/tenancy documents if housing-related (agreements, notices, rents paid)
- Demand letters, prior dispute-resolution correspondence, prior settlement offers
- Chronology/timeline of events (short, dated bullet timeline)
- Names and contact info for witnesses and any pot

ential expert(s)
- Photographs, repair estimates, property inspection reports (if applicable)
- Court papers you’ve already received or filed (complaint, answer, motions, notices) and the case number/judge name
- Retainer agreement / fee arrangement (if you already engaged Sarah)

What the court typically wants at a status conference
- Confirmation the parties are properly served and that all parties/counsel are present or represented
- A short statement of the case and the key disputed issues
- Proposed sc

hedule for discovery, motions, expert disclosures, and trial date
- Estimate of trial length and whether the case is ready for settlement talks/mediation
- Identification of any motions needing early resolution or requests for temporary relief
- Orders setting deadlines and management of the case going forward

Typical next steps after a status conference (what to expect)
- Court issues a scheduling order (deadlines for discovery, expert disclosures, motion cutoffs, pretrial dates)
- Parties serve discovery

(interrogatories, requests for production, subpoenas) and start depositions if needed
- Potential motion practice (motions to compel, dispositive motions) depending on facts and legal issues
- Settlement discussions and/or court-ordered mediation at some point before trial
- Pretrial disclosures and exchange of exhibits/witness lists
- Trial or alternative resolution (settlement, dismissal, summary judgment)
- If judgment entered, post‑judgment collection/enforcement or post‑trial motions/appeal

Practical

preservation steps to take immediately
- Save and back up all relevant electronic communications (email, text messages, chat logs); export and archive them
- Preserve relevant financial records and bank statements (download PDFs)
- Do not delete anything related to the dispute or discuss strategy with non‑lawyer third parties
- Make a concise, dated timeline of events and identify the strongest 3–5 documents that prove your case

How evidence is typically handled (useful to ask about)
- Authentication: how

to authenticate emails and business records (affidavits, custodians of records)
- Hearsay concerns: which documents may need live testimony or business-records exception
- Admissibility and exhibit preparation for the court

Issues specific to Maricopa County / Arizona (ask your lawyer to confirm)
- Local court protocols for the specific court handling your matter (Justice Court vs Superior Court vs Housing Court)
- Whether local rules require a joint status report or form scheduling order
- Any local alte

rnative dispute resolution (ADR) program availability or mandatory mediation rules

Questions to ask about strategy and settlement posture
- Given the facts, do we pursue aggressive litigation or early settlement?
- What are the strengths and weaknesses of our position and theirs?
- What settlement range is realistic and what would be acceptable to me?
- If settlement, should we include confidentiality, non‑disparagement, or non‑compete terms?

If you want, I can:
- Turn these into a concise checklist/email

you can send to Sarah (I can draft that message for you),
- Or make a one‑page timeline document you can bring to the meeting,
- Or help you draft a preservation email to key custodians to prevent spoliation.

Which would you like next? Also confirm: is this actually a landlord/tenant housing court matter, or is “housing court” the venue name for something else?
